00.intro: You are registering one agent in the agent inventory, the record that is the source of truth for its autonomy tier. The tier you set here drives everything downstream: the CI pipeline reads it to select the control profile (05), the identity issuer refuses a workload identity to any agent without an entry, and G0 checks that risk and compliance concur with the proposed tier.
tips: Keep this separate from the model inventory: the underlying model is registered there as a vendor model with a version, and this entry points to it.
Propose the tier from impact (domain, data, external access, scope, reversibility) and likelihood (autonomy, task complexity, exposure), per IMDA §2.1.1.
A first go-live is at T2 or below unless G4 evidence already exists, so an intake proposal of T3 or T4 needs a stated route to get there.
Update this entry on any change of tier, owner, model or status; a tier change is only valid after the G4 signature, never as a configuration edit.
An agent that holds a live identity but has no entry here breaks the inventory coverage metric, which targets 100%.

fields.label: Agent ID
fields.help: A stable, machine-readable identifier used in every decision record (07), the build attestation (06) and the workload identity. Lower-case with hyphens; never reuse an ID from a retired agent.

fields.label: Name
fields.help: A plain-English name a supervisor would recognise, describing the decision the agent makes rather than the technology.

fields.label: Business unit / agency
fields.help: The unit or agency whose process the agent runs and whose risk appetite applies.

fields.label: Status
fields.help: Proposed at intake; pilot while limited to test or shadow traffic; live after G3; suspended when halted by the kill switch or a gate; retired after G6.
fields.source_field: status: proposed | pilot | live | suspended | retired

fields.label: Accountable executive
fields.help: The named senior officer or system owner personally accountable for the agent's decisions. They set the tolerance, sign go-live, tier promotion and the oversight pack. Name a person, not a committee.
fields.placeholder: Jane Tan, Head of Financial Crime

fields.label: Agent owner
fields.help: The named person accountable day to day for this one agent: mandate, inventory, change and the oversight pack. Usually the product lead of the business process.

fields.label: Autonomy tier
fields.help: T1 agent proposes, human operates; T2 agent acts, human approves every significant step; T3 agent closes alone within its mandate and escalates exceptions; T4 no human in the path, oversight after the fact. RC must concur at G0.

fields.label: Why this tier
fields.help: Two or three sentences on the impact and likelihood factors behind the tier, so RC can concur or challenge at G0 and a supervisor can follow the reasoning.
fields.placeholder: High volume, reversible closures; agent closes only name-match alerts below 0.82 score; all others escalate.

fields.label: Consequence class
fields.help: The worst realistic harm of a single wrong decision to the person affected, the organisation or the public. Use the same scale as the hazard register (03).

fields.label: Reversibility
fields.help: Whether a wrong decision can be undone after it executes. Irreversible actions need significant human checkpoints (IMDA §2.2.2) and weigh heavily on the tier.

fields.label: Highest data classification
fields.help: The highest classification of any data the agent reads, retrieves or remembers, taken from the provenance record (14). The hosting must be authorised for it.

fields.label: Model(s), vendor and version
fields.help: One row per model the agent calls. Each model should also be registered in the model inventory as a vendor model with a version; a version change is a material change (G5).

fields.label: Any third-party model, platform or tool is used
fields.help: Answer yes if any model, agent platform, hosted tool or SaaS component comes from a third party. Yes makes the third-party evidence pack (16) required, opened now and complete before G3.

fields.label: The agent's own confidence decides what is auto-closed
fields.help: Answer yes if a confidence score the agent produces decides whether a case is closed or escalated. Yes makes the calibration record (10) required once four sampling rounds exist.

fields.label: Hosting
fields.help: Where the agent and its model run (on-premises, private cloud, government cloud, vendor SaaS) and in which region. It must be authorised for the highest data classification above.
fields.placeholder: Private cloud, SG region; model via vendor API

fields.label: Justification record (01)
fields.help: Reference or URL of the agent justification record. Required at G0.

fields.label: Delegation policy (02)
fields.help: Path to the mandate YAML in the agent's repository. Leave blank at intake; it must exist before G1.

fields.label: Build attestation (06)
fields.help: Registry reference of the current signed build attestation. Filled at first release and updated each release.

fields.label: Oversight pack (11)
fields.help: Reference of the tile register and generated dashboard. Must exist before G3.

fields.label: Next review
fields.help: The date this entry, the tier and the owners will next be reviewed. At most a year out; sooner for T3 and T4.

fields.label: Sunset date
fields.help: The date the agent stops unless re-approved. It should match the sunset in the mandate (02) and the exit metric in the justification (01).

01.intro: You are making the case for why this decision needs an agent rather than a rules engine, a process fix or a scorecard, in the terms the benefit will later be measured in. The accountable executive decides on it at G0, and the permanent cost of outcome sampling (09) must appear here as a line against the benefit, not be discovered in year two.
tips: Write the alternatives honestly: someone who disagrees with using an agent should be able to see which alternative was rejected and on what numbers.
Put the benefit in units you will measure at 12 months (analyst hours, cycle time), because realised versus claimed benefit is the metric for this record.
Cost sampling at the floor you expect to run permanently: at 10,000 closures a month, a 300-case floor is 3% of the work the agent removed, done by experienced reviewers.
The loop shrinks under the reduction rule but never closes, so do not assume the sampling cost falls to zero after year one.

fields.label: Decision being delegated
fields.help: The single decision the agent will take, stated as a verb and an object (for example 'close or escalate first-line name-screening alerts'), and who takes it today.

fields.label: Population
fields.help: Which cases reach the agent: case types, channels, jurisdictions and any exclusions. This becomes the sampling frame for 09.

fields.label: Monthly volume
fields.help: Expected cases per month the agent will decide. Use current operational data; it sizes both the benefit and the sampling cost.

fields.label: Alternatives and why rejected
fields.help: One row each for a deterministic rule, a process change and a scorecard at minimum. State the numbers that decided it (coverage, error rate, cost), not a preference.
fields.source_field: alternatives: deterministic rule · process change · scorecard, and why rejected

fields.label: Benefit in analyst hours
fields.help: Analyst hours per month the agent is expected to remove, net of the human time it still needs for escalations and approvals.
fields.source_field: benefit in analyst hours & cycle time

fields.label: Benefit in cycle time
fields.help: Current and expected cycle time for the decision, in the unit operations already reports.
fields.source_field: benefit in analyst hours & cycle time

fields.label: Cost of the sampling loop (09) per year
fields.help: The permanent annual cost of independent reviewers re-performing the sample. G0 checks that it is present and sits on the benefit line.
fields.source_field: cost of sampling loop (09) per year

fields.label: How the sampling cost was calculated
fields.help: Show the arithmetic: cases per month (at least the floor you expect in 02) × reviewer minutes per case × loaded hourly rate × 12, plus the full-rate rounds needed after material changes and before promotion.
fields.source_field: cost of sampling loop (09) per year

fields.label: Consequence class of a wrong decision
fields.help: The worst realistic harm of one wrong decision. It should match the class recorded in the inventory (00).
fields.source_field: consequence class of a wrong decision

fields.label: Reversibility
fields.help: Whether a wrong decision can be undone once executed, and at what effort.

fields.label: Exit / sunset metric
fields.help: The measurable condition under which the agent is switched off or not renewed, for example realised benefit below a stated share of the claim at 12 months, or disagreement above tolerance for a set number of rounds.

fields.label: Benefit review date
fields.help: When realised benefit will be compared with the claim, normally 12 months after go-live.

02.intro: You are writing the mandate: what the agent may decide alone, what it must escalate, whose authority it acts under, what it may read and touch, how it is assured and what ends it. It is the most important document in the set: the policy gate is compiled from it with no hand configuration, G1 checks that tolerance and sampling rate are written in, and 09, 10, 13 and 14 all test against it.
tips: Write it so the gate can be configured with no interpretation and a supervisor can read it and say which tier the agent sits at.
The accountable executive sets the tolerance and countersigns the tier; the framework insists a number is written down but never proposes one.
Every must_escalate condition becomes a test in 13, so phrase each one as something a test can trigger.
If confidence decides auto-closure, the threshold must point to a calibrated row in 10, not an engineer's feel.
Re-approve on every tier change and every material change; gate-config drift between this file and the running gate must be 0.

fields.label: Purpose
fields.help: One sentence stating the decision the agent disposes of, matching the justification (01).

fields.label: Authority tier
fields.help: The tier the agent operates at, which must match the inventory (00). A change of tier needs G4 and a revised mandate.

fields.label: Acts under whose authority
fields.help: The human principal or queue whose authority the agent exercises; it is carried in the identity token's delegation chain and in every decision record.

fields.label: Case types the agent may decide alone
fields.help: Only the case or alert types in scope for autonomous decision. Anything not listed escalates by default.
fields.source_field: auto-decide scope: case types, value limits, jurisdictions

fields.label: Value and score limits
fields.help: Numeric limits on autonomous decisions: amounts, match scores, counts. Each must be something the gate can check on a record field.
fields.source_field: auto-decide scope: case types, value limits, jurisdictions

fields.label: Jurisdictions and exclusions
fields.help: Jurisdictions, programmes or list entries in and out of scope for autonomous decision.
fields.placeholder: Excluded: comprehensive-sanctions programmes; PEP and adverse-media entries
fields.source_field: auto-decide scope: case types, value limits, jurisdictions

fields.label: Must-escalate conditions
fields.help: Each condition that forces escalation to a human regardless of confidence, phrased so a test can trigger it. Every one needs a passing escalation test in 13.

fields.label: Confidence routing threshold
fields.help: Only if the agent's confidence decides auto-closure: the threshold, and the 10 band it points to. Before 10 exists, state the provisional value and that it is uncalibrated.

fields.label: May read
fields.help: Every data source, corpus or memory store the agent may read. Each must resolve to a row in the provenance record (14).

fields.label: May not read
fields.help: Sources the agent is explicitly denied, even if technically reachable, such as investigator notes or suspicious-activity filings.

fields.label: Tools and permissions
fields.help: Every tool the agent may call through the gateway, with the permission and any rate or spend limit. The tool manifest hash in 06 must match this list.

fields.label: Coordination with other agents / humans
fields.help: Which agents or human teams it hands off to or receives from, over what channel, and what it may and may not accept from another agent.

fields.label: Control profile
fields.help: The 05 profile selected for this tier. It must be the profile the pipeline actually runs.
fields.source_field: assurance: control profile, sampling rate & floor, tolerance

fields.label: Sampling rate
fields.help: Share of closures independently re-performed each month by IRV, blind to the agent's answer. Required at G1 for T2 and above.
fields.source_field: assurance: control profile, sampling rate & floor, tolerance

fields.label: Sampling floor
fields.help: Minimum cases re-performed per month whatever the rate gives. 300 with zero disagreements bounds the rate at 1.0% (rule of three), the model's monthly floor for T3.
fields.source_field: assurance: control profile, sampling rate & floor, tolerance

fields.label: Tolerance (disagreement_max)
fields.help: The maximum agent-wrong disagreement rate the accountable executive will accept, compared against the Wilson interval in 09. Set by the AE; the framework never proposes a number.
fields.source_field: assurance: control profile, sampling rate & floor, tolerance

fields.label: Canary catch-rate target
fields.help: Where operators are on the loop: the share of seeded known-wrong outputs they must catch. Set here, measured monthly.

fields.label: Material-change list
fields.help: Everything whose change triggers G5: at least model version, prompt hash, tool manifest hash, rules or list version, and population shift.

fields.label: On material change
fields.help: What happens automatically: full 09 round, 10 voided, 13 regression, 03 delta, 06 re-attest.

fields.label: Re-approver
fields.help: Who re-approves on material change: the agent owner for T1–T2, risk & compliance for T3–T4 (G5).

fields.label: Sunset
fields.help: Date the mandate lapses unless re-approved; match 00.

fields.label: Mandate as YAML
fields.help: Optional: the full mandate in the repository's YAML, which the gate compiles from. Follow the structure agent, purpose, authority (tier, auto_close, must_escalate), information (may_read, may_not_read), tools, assurance (controls_profile, sampling, tolerance), evolution, sunset, as in the illustrative example.

03.intro: You are recording what can go wrong with this agent, including failures that only emerge when parts interact rather than when a part breaks. Specialists produce this register and hand it to the business to challenge; each hazard is linked to control stories (04) and controls (05), and G1 fails if any hazard has no assigned control.
tips: Do not elicit hazards from the business in a workshop; build the control structure and unsafe control actions first (STPA), then let the business challenge the result.
Read the draft from four perspectives: the attacker, a supervisor two years from now, operations at 3am, and the person who was wronged.
It is not done until at least one hazard needs two simultaneous conditions to occur; that is the sign you looked at interactions, not just components.
Use OWASP ASI01–ASI10 as prompts so goal hijack, memory poisoning and human-agent trust exploitation are not missed.
On every material change, re-run as a delta and record only what changed.

fields.label: Control structure
fields.help: The controllers (agent, gate, gateway, operators, reviewers) and the control actions and feedback between them. This is the STPA starting point that the unsafe control actions come from.

fields.label: Perspectives read
fields.help: Tick each perspective the draft has been read from before it goes to the business.
options: A supervisor two years from now

fields.label: ASI categories considered
fields.help: The OWASP ASI 2026 categories used as prompts. A category left unticked should be explained in a hazard or a note.

fields.label: Delta against
fields.help: For a re-run after material change: the change and the previous register version this is a delta against.

fields.label: Hazard register
fields.help: One row per hazard. Loss is what is harmed; the unsafe control action is what the agent or a controller does or fails to do; the causal scenario is how it happens. Tick interaction when two or more simultaneous conditions are needed.

columns.label: Needs two or more simultaneous conditions

04.intro: You are writing each control as a backlog story with acceptance criteria, in the same backlog, estimate and demo as the feature work. Stories are derived from the hazard register (03) and the control catalogue (05), labelled with the control ID; G2 checks they are accepted and the pipeline tests are green.
tips: Don't invent controls per project: start from the tier profile in 05 and the controls assigned in 03.
Requirements in a non-functional annex have no owner, estimate, test or demo, and they are the first thing dropped when a date slips.
Write the observable behaviour as Given / When / Then so the acceptance test follows directly from it.
Demonstrate control stories at sprint review alongside feature stories, and track how many of each are deferred per release.

fields.label: Control stories
fields.help: One row per control story. The acceptance test must be one the pipeline runs, and the evidence must name the record and field that proves the control ran.

fields.label: Story detail (Gherkin)
fields.help: Optional: the full text of one or more stories in Given / When / Then form, with Evidence and Test lines, as in the AGT-014 example.

fields.label: Control stories deferred this release
fields.help: Count of control stories moved out of the release. Compared with feature stories deferred, it shows whether controls are the first thing dropped.

fields.label: Feature stories deferred this release
fields.help: Count of feature stories moved out of the same release.

05.intro: You are maintaining the controls as data: each with its applicability, a deterministic test, the evidence it emits and its on-fail action, cut into one profile per tier. This is the reusable, organisation-wide asset: the CI pipeline selects the profile from the inventory tier (00) and runs every test, control stories (04) reference its IDs, and G2 fails closed on any block_deploy control.
tips: Don't write a house catalogue: seed from CSA AICM v1.1 and ISO 42001 Annex A, because the mappings are the asset and a house catalogue throws them away.
A test is deterministic only if it runs without a human interpreting anything; a checker that reasons probabilistically is itself an ungoverned model.
Use block_deploy for controls whose absence makes the agent unsafe to ship, block_action for per-action checks at the gate, and alert only where a human follow-up is enough.
Version the catalogue like code; the profile is selected per agent at every build.

fields.label: Seed catalogues
fields.help: The published catalogues imported. For public-sector deployments, import the GenAI SSP as a profile.
options: SG GenAI SSP (DP-8, GA-1 to GA-8)

fields.label: Catalogue version
fields.help: The version tag of the catalogue repository this profile is cut from.

fields.label: Profile tier
fields.help: The tier this profile serves. One profile per tier, so selection is a lookup from the inventory tier.

fields.label: Controls
fields.help: One row per control in the profile. applies_to states tier, data class and consequence class; test is an expression the pipeline evaluates; evidence names record type and field.

columns.label: Applies to (tier, data class, consequence class)
columns.source_field: applies_to: tier, data class, consequence class

columns.label: Maps to
columns.source_field: maps_to: AICM · ISO 42001 · IMDA · IM8/SSP · AI Act

fields.label: Controls as YAML / OSCAL
fields.help: Optional: the profile as it sits in the OSCAL repository, one entry per control with id, title, applies_to, test, evidence, on_fail and maps_to.

06.intro: You are describing exactly what this release of the agent is, in a form a machine can check, and signing it; this applies to every release, including prompt-only ones. It lets any decision record (07) be resolved to the exact build that made it, feeds the version-drift check and G5 change detection, and is required at G3 alongside the 13 report and 16 evidence it references.
tips: A prompt-only change is still a release and still changes the prompt hash, so it needs a new attestation.
The version triple here (model version, prompt hash, tool manifest hash) must match what appears on every 07 record; any mismatch is version drift and is red.
Only mark a control inherited from platform when the matching 16 row carries evidence.
Express components as OSCAL component-definitions so the controls they satisfy map straight to 05.

fields.label: Agent ID
fields.help: Must match the inventory (00).

fields.label: Release version
fields.help: The release tag this attestation signs.

fields.label: Prompt-only release
fields.help: Yes if only the prompt changed. It still needs attestation and still triggers G5.

fields.label: Model vendor
fields.help: Vendor of the model in force for this release.

fields.label: Model version
fields.help: Exact model version string as recorded on 07 records.

fields.label: Prompt hash
fields.help: Hash of the full system prompt and templates as deployed.

fields.label: Tool manifest hash
fields.help: Hash of the tool manifest below.

fields.label: Tool manifest
fields.help: The manifest (for example MCP tool manifests) listing every tool, matching 02 tools & permissions.

fields.label: Identity (SPIFFE ID)
fields.help: The agent's workload identity. Issued only if an inventory entry exists.

fields.label: Gateway endpoint
fields.help: The tool gateway endpoint all external calls go through; there must be no other path.

fields.label: Controls satisfied by component
fields.help: One row per component and control it satisfies. Inherited-from-platform rows need a 16 evidence reference.

fields.label: SBOM reference
fields.help: Location of the software bill of materials for this build.

fields.label: Provenance signature
fields.help: Reference to the SLSA / in-toto provenance signature proving the running build is this build.

fields.label: 13 report reference
fields.help: The pre-deployment evaluation or regression report for this release.

fields.label: 16 evidence references
fields.help: References to third-party evidence rows relied on by this release. Leave empty only if no third party is used.

07.intro: You are confirming the platform emits a conformant decision record for every action: one record per action, sealed before execution, with inputs, tool calls, structured grounds, gate verdict and version triple. Records are never written by a person; this form attests that the emitter does it. The records feed sampling (09), the version-drift check against 06, the oversight pack (11) and G3, which requires 07 emitting.
tips: A record written after the action is a different and lesser thing; confirm it is sealed before the core system is called.
Grounds must be structured fields a script can re-check; the free-text rationale is kept but nothing relies on it.
The test is whether a record from eighteen months ago can be pulled, its chain verified, its version triple resolved and its grounds re-checked with nobody who built the agent in the room.
Pin OpenTelemetry GenAI attribute names, since the conventions are still in development status.

fields.label: Record store
fields.help: The append-only store the records go to.

fields.label: Sealed before execution
fields.help: Yes only if the record is written and sealed before the tool gateway calls the core system.

fields.label: Merkle anchoring per batch
fields.help: Optional anchoring of record batches (RFC 6962).

fields.label: record_id
fields.help: Unique ID per action.

fields.label: prev_hash
fields.help: Hash of the previous record, forming the chain.

fields.label: agent_id
fields.help: Matches the inventory (00).

fields.label: principal {human, act}
fields.help: The human principal and the agent's identity acting on their behalf (act claim).

fields.label: versions {model, prompt_hash, tool_manifest_hash}
fields.help: The version triple, which must match the 06 attestation.

fields.label: inputs_read[]
fields.help: Every input the agent read, by identifier.

fields.label: tool_calls[]
fields.help: Every tool call made.

fields.label: proposed_action
fields.help: The action the agent proposed to the gate.

fields.label: grounds {structured fields, rule_id, confidence}
fields.help: Matched and unmatched fields, deltas, rule ID and confidence as structured fields.

fields.label: rationale_text (kept, not relied on)
fields.help: Free-text rationale, stored but never used by any check.

fields.label: gate {decision, policy_version, checks}
fields.help: The gate's allow / block / escalate verdict and the 02 policy version.

fields.label: outcome
fields.help: Whether and how the action executed.

fields.label: hash
fields.help: SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 canonicalised record.

fields.label: sig
fields.help: Signature over the record by the emitter's key.

fields.label: Sample record
fields.help: Paste one real (redacted) record so reviewers can see the fields populated.

fields.label: Record completeness (worst day)
fields.help: Actions with a chain-verified record and all grounds fields, divided by actions, on the worst day of the period. Threshold ≥ 99.9%.

fields.label: Chain verification
fields.help: Records re-hashed and verified divided by records, nightly. Threshold 100%.

08.intro: You are confirming the platform emits one dull, identical record shape for every control run, stored as OSCAL assessment-results. This is what lets one query answer 'every agent in the organisation, status today': the oversight pack (11) is generated from these records, and control-test coverage and evidence freshness are computed from them.
tips: Keep the shape identical across teams; two teams' agents should appear in the same table without translation.
Population tested and exceptions count matter as much as pass or fail; a pass over an empty population is not evidence.
Evidence pointers should resolve to 07 records or pipeline artefacts, not to documents.

fields.label: Assessment-results store
fields.help: Where the OSCAL assessment-results are written.

fields.label: control_id
fields.help: The 05 control ID.

fields.label: agent_id
fields.help: Matches the inventory (00).

fields.label: period
fields.help: The period or build the run covers.

fields.label: result: pass | fail | not-applicable
fields.help: One of the three values only.

fields.label: population tested
fields.help: How many items the test ran over.

fields.label: exceptions count
fields.help: Items that failed within the population.

fields.label: evidence pointer(s)
fields.help: Pointers to the 07 records or artefacts examined.

fields.label: run_id
fields.help: Unique ID of the control run.

fields.label: hash
fields.help: Hash of the record for integrity.

fields.label: Sample record
fields.help: Paste one real record.

fields.label: Evidence freshness (worst control)
fields.help: Age in days of the latest passing result for the stalest control.

fields.label: Oversight pack generated by query
fields.help: Yes if 11 is produced from these records without hand assembly.

09.intro: You are fixing the sampling method and recording the results of independent reviewers re-performing a stratified random sample of the agent's closures, blind to its answer. It is the only artefact that says anything about whether decisions were right: the disagreement rate and its Wilson interval are compared to the tolerance in 02, feed the Outcome tiles in 11, the calibration record (10), and four consecutive in-tolerance full-rate rounds are required for G4.
tips: Fix the method (frame, strata, sample rule, disagreement definition) before any results are known, and log the selection seed.
Always report the worst stratum with the overall rate: a 1% overall rate that is 9% in one stratum is a 9% problem.
Only agent-wrong counts against the agent; reviewer-wrong is a competence finding and both-defensible goes back to the mandate (02).
Never use an LLM judge for the outcome number; judges share the agent's blind spots and may only triage which records a human sees first.
At T2, human approval already reviews 100% of actions, but still sample the approvals to detect rubber-stamping.

fields.label: Date method fixed
fields.help: The date this plan was locked. It must precede the first result it governs.

fields.label: Sampling frame (from 07)
fields.help: Every closure in the period, drawn from the 07 store, so the frame is itself evidenced. State the query or filter.

fields.label: Strata
fields.help: Stratify by stated confidence band, case type and the category where systematic error is most likely; add jurisdiction or channel where volumes justify it.
fields.source_field: strata: confidence band · case type · risk category · jurisdiction

fields.label: Risk category and stratum definitions
fields.help: Name the category where systematic error is most likely (for example transliteration or script class, or self-employed income) and define each stratum's boundaries.
fields.source_field: strata: confidence band · case type · risk category · jurisdiction

fields.label: Sample size and rule
fields.help: The rate and floor from 02 and how n is allocated to strata. For reference, zero disagreements in 300 bounds the rate at 1.0%; 1,000 bounds it at 0.3%, the size for post-change and promotion rounds.

fields.label: Selection seed (logged)
fields.help: The random seed and where it is logged. Independent review makes the selection from the record store.

fields.label: Reviewer roster and competence
fields.help: Everyone who re-performs cases, with their competence and confirmation they are independent of the agent owner.

fields.label: Reviewers are blind to agent output
fields.help: Yes only if reviewers cannot see the agent's decision, grounds or confidence while re-performing.

fields.label: Disagreement definition (pre-set)
fields.help: Set before the round. The model's definition: the reviewer would not have closed, or would have closed on grounds that change the risk class.

fields.label: Classification rules
fields.help: How each disagreement is classified as agent wrong, reviewer wrong or both defensible, and who adjudicates.
fields.source_field: classification: agent wrong · reviewer wrong · both defensible

fields.label: Sampling rounds
fields.help: One row per round. Enter counts; the app computes the rate and Wilson 95% interval overall and for the worst stratum. Full rate is required after material change and before promotion.

columns.label: Agent wrong
columns.source_field: classification: agent wrong · reviewer wrong · both defensible

columns.label: Reviewer wrong
columns.source_field: classification: agent wrong · reviewer wrong · both defensible

columns.label: Both defensible
columns.source_field: classification: agent wrong · reviewer wrong · both defensible

fields.source_field: results: rate + Wilson 95% overall & by stratum, worst stratum

fields.label: Re-baseline triggers fired
fields.help: Material changes or population shifts in the period that forced a full-rate round or reset. Write 'none' if none.

fields.label: Strata with no sample this quarter
fields.help: Strata with closures but no 09 sample; they feed the Unknown tile in 11.

10.intro: You are showing whether the agent's confidence bands mean what they claim, using the 09 results per band. Wherever the agent's own confidence decides what is auto-closed, the routing threshold in the mandate (02) must point at a calibrated row here rather than an engineer's feel; it is opened after four sampling rounds, supports G4, and is voided by any material change (G5).
tips: Open it only after at least four sampling rounds; fewer rounds cannot show a band is stable.
Judge each band on its interval, not its point estimate, against the tolerance in 02.
A band moves to a reduced rate only after four consecutive in-tolerance rounds at the full rate, with a floor of 300 per band per quarter.
Any material change voids calibration and returns every band to the full rate; the loop shrinks but never closes.

fields.label: Confidence bands
fields.help: How the confidence range is cut into bands, and which band is never auto-closed.

fields.label: Per-band results
fields.help: One row per band, cumulative over the rounds held. The app computes the observed rate and Wilson interval from sampled and disagreements.
fields.source_field: per band: closures, sampled, disagreements, observed rate + interval

fields.label: Verdict per band
fields.help: The verdict and routing consequence for each band.

fields.label: Routing threshold
fields.help: The confidence threshold for auto-closure that 02 will reference.

fields.label: Threshold justification
fields.help: Which band rows support the threshold and why the band below it escalates.

fields.label: Rounds held
fields.help: Number of 09 rounds the per-band figures cover. Minimum four.

fields.label: Date voided
fields.help: Set when a material change voids this record. Leave blank while valid.

11.intro: You are writing the specification for the oversight dashboard, not the dashboard itself: a register of tiles, each labelled Process, Outcome or Unknown and traced to source records. It is agreed with internal and external audit and signed by the accountable executive before G3; the monthly pack is then generated from it by query and re-signed after every full sampling round (09).
tips: Every tile states its kind; a Process tile says the control ran, an Outcome tile says the decision was right, and neither may be read as a safety number without saying so.
An Unknown tile is mandatory: name the strata and closures with no 09 sample this period.
Show tails, not means; an average hides the worst day and the worst stratum.
Every outcome tile shows its provenance: population, n, who reviewed, period and interval.
Business and technical views must reconcile to the same records; at maturity L3, the pack should say it has no outcome evidence yet.

fields.label: Register version
fields.help: The version of this tile register being signed.

fields.label: Date agreed with audit
fields.help: When internal (and, where relevant, external) audit agreed the register. Must precede G3.

fields.label: Tiles
fields.help: One row per tile. Source record must be 07, 08, 09 or 10; provenance is mandatory for outcome tiles; aggregation states the tail used.

columns.label: Provenance (outcome tiles)
columns.source_field: provenance (outcome tiles): population, n, who, period, interval

fields.label: An Unknown tile is present
fields.help: Yes only if at least one tile reports what has not been tested.

fields.label: Pack generated by query without manual steps
fields.help: Yes if the monthly pack is produced from 07/08/09/10 by query with no hand assembly.

fields.label: Business and technical views reconcile
fields.help: Yes if both views are computed from the same records.

12.intro: You are writing the runbook for when things change or go wrong: what counts as a material change, how incidents that are wrong actions (not outages) are contained, who holds the kill switch and how fast it must work, and how the agent is retired. It is required at G3 with a drill inside the time limit, drives G5 revalidation and G6 decommissioning, and drill records feed the oversight pack (11).
tips: Write incident response for actions, not outages: the agent may be perfectly available while closing the wrong cases.
Containment order is revoke identity, disable tools at the gateway, then halt; a dashboard is not a kill switch.
The last drill must have halted the agent inside the stated time, and the drill record must be in the oversight pack.
Drill quarterly for T3 and T4; track change-to-revalidation days against the 30-day threshold.

fields.label: Material-change definition
fields.help: What counts as material, matching the 02 evolution list: model version, prompt hash, tool manifest, rules or list version, population shift, and any 14 source change.

fields.label: Approval path
fields.help: Who approves a material change at G5: the agent owner for T1–T2, risk & compliance for T3–T4, and how drift on 07 triggers it automatically.

fields.label: Revalidation trigger
fields.help: What runs after a material change: full 09 round, 10 voided, 13 regression, 03 delta, 06 re-attest.

fields.label: Maximum days to completed revalidation
fields.help: Days from material change to a completed full 09 round. The metric threshold is 30 days or fewer.

fields.label: Incident classes
fields.help: At least one row each for wrong action, compromise and drift, with how it is detected and the first response.
fields.source_field: incident classes: wrong action · compromise · drift

fields.label: Reversal and customer / citizen remediation

fields.label: Regulator notification decision tree
fields.help: Which incidents are notified to whom, by when, and who decides.

13.intro: You are reporting the evidence that the agent behaves as the mandate (02) says before real cases reach it: whole workflows, tool calls, robustness and red-team results. The report is attached to the build attestation (06), is required at G3 and is re-run as a regression suite on every material change; for T3 and T4, independent review runs or witnesses it.
tips: Every must_escalate condition in 02 needs a passing test proving the agent escalates; the target is 100%.
Test whole workflows, not just final outputs, in an environment as close to production as you can get, and repeat runs to see variance.
Every red-team finding must end fixed, accepted by the agent owner, or linked to a control.
A test set isn't the production population: 13 is necessary but it can't substitute for outcome sampling (09).

fields.label: Scope
fields.help: The IMDA §2.3.2 dimensions covered. All four are expected; explain any gap under known limitations.
fields.source_field: scope: task execution · policy compliance · tool-calling accuracy · robustness

fields.label: Workflow-level tests
fields.help: The end-to-end workflows tested, from input through tool calls to the action and its decision record.

fields.label: Multi-agent tests
fields.help: Tests of hand-offs to and from other agents, including malformed or hostile messages. Write 'not applicable' with a reason if the agent works alone.

fields.label: Environment realism
fields.help: How the test environment differs from production (data, tools, latency, permissions) and why the results still hold.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.help: Datasets used, their size, how they were built and how they differ from the production population.

fields.label: Repeat count
fields.help: How many times each test was run, so non-determinism is visible in the intervals.

fields.label: Independent review ran or witnessed the evaluation
fields.help: Required yes for T3 and T4.

fields.label: Litmus run IDs
fields.help: Government deployments: the GovTech Litmus run IDs for this evaluation.

fields.label: Pass criteria (from 02)
fields.help: The thresholds the agent must meet, taken from the mandate, stated before the results are run.

fields.label: Escalation-condition tests
fields.help: One row per must_escalate condition in 02, with the test that proves the agent escalates and whether it passed.

fields.label: Results with intervals
fields.help: One row per measure. Always give n and an interval, not a point estimate.

fields.label: Red-team results by ASI01–ASI10
fields.help: One row per finding, grouped by ASI category. Disposition must be fixed, accepted by the AOW, or linked to a control.

fields.label: Known limitations
fields.help: What this evaluation cannot show, including where the test population differs from production. These feed the Unknown tile in 11.

14.intro: You are recording everything the agent reads, retrieves and remembers: every source, corpus and memory store, with its classification, owner and version. The data owner approves it; every item in the mandate's may_read (02) must resolve to a row here, and the highest classification feeds the inventory (00). Memory and retrieval corpora are attack surface as well as data.
tips: Start from 02 may_read and add a row for each item; any may_read item without a row fails the metric, whose target is 0.
Check each classification against what the hosting location is authorised for, not just what the data owner would like.
Name every path by which content is written into memory or a corpus; those are the poisoning routes (ASI06).
A change to any source, corpus version or memory store is a material change, so version and snapshot identifiers matter.

fields.label: Sources, corpora and memory stores
fields.help: One row per item. Version / snapshot should be an identifier that appears in 06 or 07, so a decision can be tied to the data it saw.

fields.label: Every 02 may_read item has a row here
fields.help: Yes only when every entry in 02 may_read resolves to a row with an owner and a classification the hosting is authorised for.

fields.label: Hosting authorisation reference
fields.help: The authorisation that permits the hosting for the highest classification here (for government, the relevant GenAI SSP DP-8 / GA environment authorisation).

15.intro: You are writing for two audiences: the people affected by the agent, who must be told they are dealing with one, what it can decide and how to reach a human; and the operators, who must be trained on its failure modes and on how to approve, override and halt it. It is required at G3, and operator training currency and the canary catch rate feed the oversight pack (11).
tips: Test the notice in the channel the user actually uses: can they find out an agent acted and how to reach a person there?
Oversight that isn't trained is a rubber stamp; cover automation bias explicitly, not just the mechanics of the screen.
Derive the failure modes for operators from the hazard register (03) and known limitations in 13.
Refresh on material change and run refreshers on the stated cadence; lapsed training lowers the operators-trained figure.

fields.label: Where the notice is published
fields.help: The channel(s) and URL or screen where affected people see the notice.

fields.label: Declares agent interaction
fields.help: The exact wording telling people they are dealing with an agent, and at which point in the journey it appears.

fields.label: Range of actions & decisions
fields.help: In plain language, what the agent can decide or do for them, consistent with 02 auto-decide scope.

fields.label: Data handling
fields.help: What data the agent uses about them and how it is kept, consistent with 14.

fields.label: Human escalation points
fields.help: How a person reaches a human, and when the agent hands over automatically.

fields.label: User responsibilities
fields.help: What users must do or check themselves, including acknowledging the risk of wrong or invented output where relevant (GenAI SSP GA-8).

fields.label: Failure modes operators must recognise
fields.help: The ways this agent goes wrong that an operator can spot, with an example of each.
fields.source_field: operator: failure modes · approve / override / halt · automation-bias training · refresher cadence

fields.help: Step-by-step for each, including who may pull the kill switch and the time-to-halt limit in 12.

fields.label: Automation-bias training
fields.help: What the training does to counter over-reliance on the agent, such as seeded known-wrong cases (canaries).
fields.source_field: operator: failure modes · approve / override / halt · automation-bias training · refresher cadence

fields.label: Refresher cadence
fields.help: How often operators repeat training. Also refresh on every material change.

fields.help: Number of on-the-loop or in-the-loop operators who need current training.

fields.label: Operators with current training
fields.help: Share of operators in scope whose training is current, from LMS records. G3 expects every on-the-loop operator's training to be current.

16.intro: You are collecting the evidence behind every control a model vendor or agent platform claims to handle for this agent. A claim is an assertion until evidence is attached: the build attestation (06) may only mark a control 'inherited from platform' when a row here carries the evidence, and G1 expects this pack opened while G3 expects it complete.
tips: Treat marketing pages and questionnaire answers as claims, not evidence; the source reference found only 4 of 30 deployed agentic systems publish a safety system card.
Check the scope of each certification or report: a certificate that covers the vendor's hosting but not the model endpoint you call does not evidence the claim.
For vendor SaaS, confirm you can export records you can chain and sample yourself, otherwise 07 and 09 cannot be run on your terms.
Where the policy gate lives when the agent is vendor SaaS is an open question in the model; write down your answer rather than leaving it implicit.
Refresh the pack on any vendor change, which is also a material change under G5.

fields.label: Vendors and components
fields.help: One row per third-party model, platform, tool host or SaaS component the agent depends on, with the version in use.

fields.label: Controls claimed (by 05 id)
fields.help: Every control in the catalogue (05) the vendor says it satisfies on your behalf, one control ID per line.

fields.label: Evidence per claim
fields.help: One row per claimed control. 'None yet' is allowed while the pack is open but must be cleared before G3. Scope states exactly what the evidence covers.
fields.source_field: evidence per claim: test report | attestation | certification + scope

fields.label: No training on our data
fields.help: Yes only if the contract binds the provider not to log, store or train on your data (compare SG GenAI SSP GA-3).
